lead_with.title: A CFO's cost case
lead_with.text: Finance Montréal's Boyd Company model puts a 150-person support centre at about **US$18.9M a year in Montréal vs US$35.3M in New York**, with payroll at about 56% of New York's. Lead with numbers, not with promotion.

company.text: Assurant Japan was established in **August 2016** as the Japanese arm of Assurant, Inc. It started with **smartphone warranties** and now covers the whole device lifecycle: trade-in and upgrade programs, **AI- and robotics-based device processing**, sale of refurbished phones, and repairs through **Yuu Solutions**, which joined the group and operates about **150 in-store repair locations**. It also offers appliance extended warranties with technical support, built on the **Torisetsu** appliance-manual app. The company celebrated its **10th anniversary in August 2026**. Its parent, Assurant, is a US provider of device protection, vehicle protection, renters and lender-placed housing insurance, operating in 21 countries. In Canada, Assurant has its **headquarters in Toronto** and a vehicle-protection office in **Hamilton**; it acquired the Canadian cellular repair centre **All Tech Neek Electronics (2019)** and **Coast To Coast Dealer Services (2015)**. A Montréal presence was **not found** (to be confirmed).

financials.text: **Assurant, Inc. FY2025:** total revenue **$12.81B** (vs $11.88B in 2024); net income **$872.7M** (+15%); adjusted EBITDA **$1.54B** (+16%); adjusted EPS **$19.77** (+19%). **Global Lifestyle** (device and vehicle protection, where Japan sits) earned **$9.58B** in premiums, fees and other income (+7%), adjusted EBITDA $801M. **Global Housing** adjusted EBITDA $859M (+28%). Capital returned to shareholders in 2025: **$468M**. 2026 outlook: Global Lifestyle adjusted EBITDA expected up **high single digits**. Assurant Japan's own figures are **not published**.

industry.title: Device protection keeps growing
industry.text: Assurant's 2025 growth in Global Lifestyle was driven by **global mobile programs**; Japan is one of those markets (warranties, trade-in, refurbishment).

industry.title: Insurers look for lower-cost hubs
industry.text: Large financial groups put finance, compliance, IT and claims work in support centres. Montréal positions itself as **about 51% cheaper than New York** for such centres, including the IFC credit.

industry.title: Québec IFC tax credit
industry.text: Companies running an **International Financial Centre** in greater Montréal can get a credit of **up to C$18,000 per eligible employee per year**, including for **outsourced services to a foreign affiliated financial entity** (compliance, corporate finance and tax, IT). Eligibility of insurance activities **to be confirmed** with Finance Montréal's IFC team.

talking_points: Congratulate him on **Assurant Japan's 10 years** (August 2026) and on getting through the Q3 close.
How does Assurant organise **finance, actuarial and shared services** globally today: where are the hubs, and who decides on new locations?
Is **Assurant Canada (Toronto)** growing, and does the group look at **bilingual capacity** for North America?
Would a short **cost comparison** (Montréal vs New York/Toronto, with the IFC credit) be useful to share with group finance?
Who in **Assurant's US or Canadian leadership** should Finance Montréal meet next, and would Yoshi make the introduction?
